name: Xero

composio.note: Composio has no managed Xero app. You register your own Xero Web app, then paste its client ID and secret into a Composio auth config. Every connection counts against your own Xero app's tier and connection cap, and your Xero bill.

verdict.headline: Credentials take 15 minutes, but new apps start capped at 5 connected orgs. Up to 50 needs a paid tier; beyond that you need Xero certification.
verdict.summary: Creating a Xero Web app is self-serve with no review, so a developer can connect their own demo company the same day. Since 2 March 2026 every app starts on the free Starter tier (5 connections, 1,000 calls/day per org). Adding a credit card moves you to Core (50 connections, $35 AUD/month). Going past 50 connections needs app certification (Plus tier, $245 AUD/month), and Xero publishes no review timeline. The developer terms ban training AI/ML models on Xero API data.

toProduction.label: Same day for ≤50 orgs (Core); about 3–12 weeks for >50 (certification)

activeEffort.label: 1–2 hours to first connection; 2–6 days to build certification requirements

approval.name: Xero app certification (App Partner, Plus tier and above)
approval.trigger: More than 50 connected organisations, or a Xero App Store listing. Up to 5 is free (Starter); 6–50 only needs a credit card (Core). Advanced/Enterprise and premium endpoints (Journals, XPM, bulk connections) also need a security assessment and use-case approval.
approval.wait: Not published by Xero. Community and vendor guides report weeks to several months (inferred).

prerequisites.text: A free Xero account, with the Xero Demo Company enabled for testing.
Accept the Xero Developer Platform Terms (updated 4 December 2025; they apply to all developers from 2 March 2026).
A credit card on file once you need a 6th connection. Credit card is the only accepted payment method.
A Composio project where you can create an auth config.

oauth.refreshTokens: Access token: 30 minutes. Refresh token: 60 days, only if you request `offline_access`. Every refresh returns a new refresh token (rotation); save both. If you lose the response you can retry with the old refresh token for a 30-minute grace period, then it is dead and the user must re-authorise. Auth codes expire after 5 minutes and are single-use.
oauth.redirectUriRules: Must be https, except `http://localhost`. `http://127.0.0.1` is not allowed. Custom URL schemes are not supported (PKCE apps). Must match the URI registered on the app. SPAs are not supported for PKCE.

steps.title: Create a Xero account and enable the Demo Company
steps.detail: Sign up for a free Xero account and turn on the Demo Company. You test against it at no cost.

steps.title: Create a Web app in the developer portal
steps.detail:
In My Apps, click **New app**. Pick **Web app** (Auth Code grant). Composio needs a client secret, so do not pick PKCE (no secret) or Custom connection (client credentials, single org).

- App name: your product name. Certification rejects names containing "Xero".
- Company or application URL: your site.
- Redirect URI: the one Composio shows (next steps).

steps.title: Generate the client secret
steps.detail: On the app page, click **Generate a secret**. Copy the client ID and secret into a secret manager.

steps.title: Create the auth config in Composio
steps.detail:
Composio dashboard → **Create Auth Config** → toolkit **Xero** → auth type **OAuth2** (not Bearer) → check **Use your own developer authentication** → paste client ID and secret.

Scopes: always include `offline_access`. Use granular scopes (e.g. `accounting.invoices`, `accounting.payments`) instead of the broad `accounting.transactions` that Composio's guide lists. New apps get granular scopes.

steps.title: Add Composio's redirect URI to the Xero app
steps.detail: Copy the redirect URI the Composio dashboard shows and add it to the Xero app. Composio's Xero guide shows `https://backend.composio.dev/api/v3/toolkits/auth/callback` (no trailing slash). Older Composio guides show `https://backend.composio.dev/api/v1/auth-apps/add`. The dashboard is authoritative.

steps.title: Connect your Demo Company and read the tenant ID
steps.detail: Start a connection from Composio and sign in to Xero. On the consent screen, pick the Demo Company. Then call `GET https://api.xero.com/connections` (Composio tool `XERO_GET_CONNECTIONS`) and note `tenantId`. Filter by `?authEventId=` (from the access token JWT) to see only orgs connected in this flow.

steps.title: Wire tenant selection and rate-limit handling
steps.detail:
- Send `xero-tenant-id: <tenantId>` on every API call. One user can connect several orgs, so store the chosen tenant per connected account.
- On HTTP 429, read `X-Rate-Limit-Problem` and wait `Retry-After` seconds for that tenant.
- Batch up to ~50 items per POST/PUT.

steps.title: Add a credit card before your 6th connection
steps.detail: Starter allows 5 connections. Add payment details in the developer portal to move to Core: 50 connections, $35 AUD/month, 10 GB egress, then $2.40 AUD/GB. Daily limit rises from 1,000 to 5,000 calls per org.

steps.title: Build the certification requirements
steps.detail:
Xero reviews against checkpoints, including:

- A setup page showing the connected tenant name and status, with connect and disconnect buttons.
- Disconnect via `DELETE /connections/{id}`; handle disconnects made from Xero's side.
- A Login URL for the App Launcher in the app configuration.
- Minimal scopes with a stated use for each; `offline_access` is required.
- User-facing error messages, account and tax-rate mapping if you write data.
- No pop-ups for the OAuth redirect; no secrets in the frontend.

steps.title: Apply to move to Plus (certification)
steps.detail: Apply in the developer portal to move tiers. Once certified you move to Plus: 1,000 connections, $245 AUD/month, optional App Store listing. Xero recommends having about 10 beta customers first. You stay capped at 50 connections until approved.

steps.title: Wait for Xero's certification review
steps.detail: Xero does not publish a timeline. Vendor and community guides report weeks to several months. Expect follow-up questions about scopes and use cases.

steps.title: Each customer org authorises the connection
steps.detail: A user of the customer's Xero org consents and picks which orgs to connect. Until you are certified, each org can connect at most five uncertified apps, so a busy org may need to remove one. For cashbook/ledger (partner edition) orgs, practice staff must authorise.

scopes.name: offline_access
scopes.purpose: Returns a refresh token. Without it the connection dies after 30 minutes. Required for certification.

scopes.name: openid profile email
scopes.purpose: User identity (sign-in). Not needed for data access.

scopes.name: accounting.invoices / accounting.invoices.read
scopes.purpose: Invoices, credit notes, quotes, purchase orders, repeating invoices, items. Granular replacement for part of accounting.transactions.

scopes.name: accounting.payments / accounting.banktransactions / accounting.manualjournals (+ .read)
scopes.purpose: Payments, bank transactions and transfers, manual journals. Granular scopes.

scopes.name: accounting.reports.*.read
scopes.purpose: Granular report scopes (aged, balancesheet, banksummary, budgetsummary, executivesummary, profitandloss, trialbalance, taxreports). Replace accounting.reports.read.

scopes.name: accounting.contacts / accounting.settings / accounting.attachments (+ .read)
scopes.purpose: Contacts, org settings (accounts, tax rates, tracking), attachments.

scopes.name: accounting.transactions / accounting.reports.read
scopes.purpose: Deprecated broad scopes. Only apps that already use them keep them until September 2027.

scopes.name: accounting.journals.read
scopes.purpose: General ledger Journals endpoint. Premium: Advanced tier, security assessment and use-case approval. Removed from new custom connections.

scopes.name: payroll.* / files / assets / projects
scopes.purpose: Payroll (AU, UK, NZ), Files, Fixed Assets, Projects APIs.

scopes.name: practicemanager.*
scopes.purpose: Xero Practice Manager. Needs app partner registration and a security self-assessment before the app can request it.

scopes.name: paymentservices / bankfeedsv2 / finance.* / accountdata.*
scopes.purpose: Only after additional certification; extra commercial agreements may apply.

gotchas.title: New apps are capped at 5 connections
gotchas.detail: Since 2 March 2026 every new app starts on Starter: 5 connected orgs and 1,000 calls/day per org. A 6th connection needs a credit card (Core, 50). Beyond 50 needs certification. You stay capped at the tier maximum until Xero approves the next tier. Every org a user ticks on the consent screen counts.

gotchas.title: Each customer org can connect only five uncertified apps
gotchas.detail: This is a per-org limit, separate from your app's cap. Accountants and busy SMBs often hit it, and only certification removes it.

gotchas.title: Refresh tokens rotate, with a 30-minute grace
gotchas.detail: Every refresh returns a new refresh token. If you lose it, the old one works for 30 more minutes, then the user must reconnect. Concurrent refreshes from parallel agent workers can race and kill the connection (inferred). Without `offline_access` there is no refresh token at all.

gotchas.title: Refresh tokens expire after 60 days unused
gotchas.detail: If nothing refreshes a connection for 60 days, it is dead. Schedule a periodic refresh for idle connections. The Organisation endpoint is excluded from egress billing, so it is a cheap keep-alive call.

gotchas.title: Every call needs `xero-tenant-id`
gotchas.detail: The access token is per user, not per org. A user can connect several orgs in one flow. Read `GET /connections`, store the right `tenantId`, and send it on every request. Agents that skip this get auth errors or hit the wrong org.

gotchas.title: Composio's guide lists broad scopes; new apps use granular ones
gotchas.detail: Composio's Xero guide suggests `accounting.transactions` and `accounting.reports.read`. Xero marks these deprecated, and apps created on or after 2 March 2026 use granular scopes. Request `accounting.invoices`, `accounting.payments`, etc. Whether Xero rejects the broad scope or silently drops it for new apps is not documented.

gotchas.title: AI/ML training on Xero data is banned
gotchas.detail: The developer terms forbid using API data, raw or processed, to train or fine-tune AI models, LLMs, or predictive analytics tools. Xero says it monitors and audits, and may suspend access. The terms also forbid bots or browser extensions that simulate user actions. Agents may use the API at runtime; do not log Xero data into training sets.

gotchas.title: Rate limits are tight per org
gotchas.detail: Per tenant: 5 concurrent calls, 60/minute, 1,000/day (Starter) or 5,000/day (Core+). App-wide: 10,000/minute. Windows reset at different times per tenant. Paid tiers also meter egress (Core 10 GB/month, then $2.40 AUD/GB).

gotchas.title: Journals endpoint is Advanced-tier only
gotchas.detail: `GET /Journals` (Composio `XERO_LIST_JOURNALS`) needs the Advanced tier, a security assessment and use-case approval. Manual journals are available on every tier.

gotchas.title: Custom connections are a different product
gotchas.detail: Custom connections use client credentials for one org, need the customer to buy a monthly subscription, and only work in AU, NZ, UK and US. They skip the 5-app limit and the new pricing. Composio's Xero OAuth2 auth config expects the auth code flow, so use a Web app (inferred).

blockers.fix: Client ID or secret is wrong, the secret was never generated, or the app is PKCE type (no secret). Regenerate the secret on a Web app and re-paste into Composio.

blockers.symptom: Authorize redirects to `login.xero.com/identity/error` instead of the consent screen
blockers.fix: Usually a bad client ID or a redirect URI that does not exactly match one registered on the app (https, no trailing slash, no 127.0.0.1). Copy the URI from the Composio dashboard into the Xero app. The probe confirmed this redirect for a fake client ID; the exact message for a URI mismatch is inferred.

You hit the tier connection cap. Add a credit card (Core, 50) or apply for certification (Plus, 1,000). Remove dead connections in the portal's Connections management page. The exact on-screen error is not documented.
Pause that tenant for `Retry-After` seconds. Check `X-MinLimit-Remaining` and `X-DayLimit-Remaining` before bursts. Upgrade from Starter if you need more than 1,000 calls/day per org.
The refresh token was rotated and the 30-minute grace passed, or it went unused for 60 days, or the user disconnected the app. The user must reconnect. Serialize refreshes per connection.

blockers.symptom: API call returns HTTP 403 (commonly `AuthenticationUnsuccessful`) right after connecting
blockers.fix: Missing or wrong `xero-tenant-id`, or the tenant was disconnected. Re-read `GET /connections` and use a current `tenantId`. Error text is from community reports.

blockers.symptom: HTTP 400: "You have reached the limit of invoices you can approve."
blockers.fix: The customer org is on a low Xero plan with an invoice cap. Not your app; the customer must upgrade their Xero plan.

objects.name: Invoices (incl. credit notes, quotes, purchase orders)
objects.description: Sales invoices and bills with line items and status
objects.note: Granular scope that replaces part of the deprecated accounting.transactions. Paged list responses include line items.

objects.name: Contacts
objects.description: Customers and suppliers with addresses and balances
objects.note: Customers and suppliers, plus contact groups.

objects.name: Bank transactions and transfers
objects.description: Money spent, received and moved between accounts
objects.note: Spend and receive money entries already in Xero. Raw bank feeds are a separate restricted API (bankfeedsv2).

objects.name: Accounts (chart of accounts)
objects.description: The ledger accounts transactions are coded to
objects.note: Comes under the settings scope, along with tax rates, currencies, items and tracking categories.

objects.name: Payments (incl. batch payments, prepayments, overpayments)
objects.description: Payments applied to invoices and bills
objects.note: Granular scope that replaces part of accounting.transactions.

objects.name: Reports (P&L, balance sheet, trial balance, aged, bank summary, tax)
objects.description: Pre-built financial reports for a date range
objects.note: One read scope per report. Request only the reports your agent uses. The broad accounting.reports.read is deprecated.

objects.name: General ledger journals
objects.description: Every ledger entry behind all transactions
objects.note: Premium. Needs the Advanced tier, a security assessment and use-case approval. Returned only in batches of 100.

changes.detail: Webhooks cover only Contact, Invoice, Credit Note, Prepayment, Overpayment and App Store Subscription events (create and update). There are none for bank transactions, payments, accounts or reports. You set one webhook per app in My Apps, with an HTTPS URL. Delivery starts only after an 'intent to receive' check: your endpoint must return 2xx for payloads correctly signed with the webhook key (HMAC-SHA256, base64, in x-xero-signature) and 401 for bad ones, within 5 seconds. Events carry IDs, not full records, so fetch the record after. Failed deliveries retry for 24 hours, then the webhook is disabled; missed events are kept up to 31 days and replayed. For everything else, poll with the If-Modified-Since header to get only records changed since your last sync. Some changes (e.g. DueDate on partly paid invoices, contact balances) do not update UpdatedDateUTC and are missed. Xero is bring-your-own on Composio, so you already use your own OAuth app; Composio documents a 15-minute minimum polling interval only for managed auth, so your own app can poll faster where the trigger supports it.

limits.text: Per connected organisation: 5 concurrent calls, 60 calls per minute, and 1,000 calls per day on the Starter tier or 5,000 per day on higher tiers. App-wide cap is 10,000 calls per minute across all organisations.
Going over a limit returns HTTP 429 with X-Rate-Limit-Problem and Retry-After headers. Responses carry X-DayLimit-Remaining and X-MinLimit-Remaining so you can pace calls.

Invoices, Contacts, CreditNotes, BankTransactions, ManualJournals, Payments, PurchaseOrders, Prepayments and Overpayments are paged with ?page=N. Page size defaults to 100, max 1,000, and a Pagination object gives the page count.
Other endpoints may need one call per record for full detail. Plan a background backfill; a first sync of a large organisation can eat most of a 1,000-call Starter day.
With 60 calls per minute per organisation, an agent answering live questions should read from a synced copy rather than call Xero on every turn.

restrictions.text: Xero API data must not be used to train, fine-tune, adapt or enhance any AI model, including LLMs. Xero says it monitors for this. Using data at runtime to answer the user's own questions is not addressed by this clause.
Use API data only for your approved use case. Do not pass it to a third party without the user's consent, and do not sell it or aggregate and supply it to another app.
Your app needs its own terms and privacy policy that state how you collect, store, use and share Xero data. Material new use cases need Xero's approval.
Sending Xero data to a third-party LLM provider may count as passing data to a third party. Get explicit user consent and check your provider does not train on it.

unknowns: How long Xero's certification review takes. Xero publishes no timeline; 3–12 weeks is an estimate from vendor guides.
The exact error a user sees when your app is at its tier connection cap.
Whether requesting broad scopes (e.g. accounting.transactions) on an app created after 2 March 2026 fails with invalid_scope or is silently dropped.
Whether Composio's dashboard currently shows the v3 callback or the older v1 redirect URI for Xero; we did not sign in.
Whether Composio refreshes Xero tokens on a schedule, which matters for the 60-day idle expiry and the rotation race.
Exact tier for apps created between 4 December 2025 and 2 March 2026 (interim billing), and details of the security assessment for Advanced.
Whether an AI agent product that only reads data at runtime triggers any extra review; the terms only ban training and UI-simulating bots.
